title: Local cancellation of one acyclic top degree of a finite locally free sheaf complex
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $r\in\mathbf Z$, and $P^\bullet$ a cochain complex of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Assume that every $P^i$ is finite locally free [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf], that $P^i=0$ for $i>r$, and that $H^r(P^\bullet)=0$, where $H^i=\ker(d^i)/\operatorname{im}(d^{i-1})$. Then for every $x\in X$ there exist an open neighbourhood $V$ of $x$, a cochain complex $Q^\bullet$ of finite locally free $\mathcal O_V$-modules with $Q^i=0$ for $i>r-1$, and a chain map $Q^\bullet\to P^\bullet|_V$ inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology sheaf. No lower bound on $P^\bullet$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08DN, lemma-finite-cohomology, proof of (1), cancellation of the top degree, also used in (2); Tag 08C6, lemma-local-lift-map, for the local section; Tag 0BCI, lemma-direct-summand-of-locally-free-is-locally-free, for the new top term. The same single-degree construction does not use boundedness below.

proof.text: Put $\delta=d^{r-1}:P^{r-1}\to P^r$. Since $P^{r+1}=0$, $d^r=0$ and hence $H^r(P)=P^r/\operatorname{im}\delta=\operatorname{Coker}\delta$. The hypothesis makes this cokernel zero. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting] (1), $\delta$ is an epimorphism and every section of $P^r$ lifts locally through it. This uses sheaf surjectivity, not surjectivity on sections of an arbitrary open.

source.place: Tag 08DN, lemma-finite-cohomology, proof (1), surjectivity of the last differential; Tag 01AF, section-kernels

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$. Apply [new-sbc-local-section-of-epi] to $\delta$ and its finite locally free target $P^r$. Obtain an open $U$ containing $x$ and $s:P^r|_U\to P^{r-1}|_U$ with $\delta s=1$. By [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf], shrink $U$ so that $A=P^{r-1}|_U$ is finite free. Write $B=P^r|_U$ and $K=\ker(\delta|_U)$, explicitly the subsheaf $W\mapsto\{a\in A(W):\delta(a)=0\}$. The kernel description is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting].

source.place: Tag 08C6, lemma-local-lift-map, applied to the identity of the locally finite free target; Tag 01C6, definition-locally-free

proof.text: Let $i:K\hookrightarrow A$. The formula $p(a)=a-s\delta(a)$ takes values in $K$, since $\delta(a-s\delta(a))=0$, and $pi=1_K$. All formulas are linear and commute with restrictions. Thus $K$ is a retract of the finite free sheaf $A$. Apply [new-pc-single-retract-sheaf-affine-trivialization] at $x$ with the open $U$ and the splitting $(i,p)$, composed with the chosen trivialization of $A$. Obtain a smaller open $V$ containing $x$ on which $K|_V$ is finite free. This supplies precisely the new finite locally free top term. The local-ring hypothesis in Tag 0BCI is satisfied because $X$ is a scheme; the cited retract theorem is already stated for schemes.

source.place: Tag 0BCI, lemma-direct-summand-of-locally-free-is-locally-free; explicit retract from the section in Tag 08DN

proof.text: On $V$ define $Q^j=P^j|_V$ for $j\le r-2$, $Q^{r-1}=K|_V$, and $Q^j=0$ for $j\ge r$. Keep the original differentials for $j\le r-3$; define $d_Q^{r-2}$ to be $d_P^{r-2}$ with codomain restricted to $K|_V$, and set all later differentials to zero. This codomain restriction is valid because $\delta d_P^{r-2}=0$. The relation $d_Q^{r-2}d_Q^{r-3}=0$ follows after the injective inclusion into $P^{r-1}|_V$; all other square-zero relations are unchanged or zero. Define $f:Q\to P|_V$ by identities in degrees $\le r-2$, the inclusion $i$ in degree $r-1$, and zero above. At degree $r-2$ the chain-map equation is the defining factorization, at degree $r-1$ it is $\delta i=0$, and elsewhere it is an identity or zero. These are exactly the complex and morphism conditions of [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Restrictions of the local trivializations in [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf] show that the unchanged terms remain finite locally free, and zero has rank zero.

source.place: Tag 08DN, lemma-finite-cohomology, proof (1), definition of the shortened complex, expanded degreewise

proof.text: For $j\le r-3$ the cycles and boundaries for $f$ are identical. In degree $r-2$, replacing the codomain of the outgoing map by its subsheaf $K|_V$ leaves its kernel unchanged, and the incoming map is unchanged, so the induced cohomology map is an isomorphism. In degree $r-1$, the cycles of $P|_V$ are exactly $K|_V$, and its boundary subsheaf is the image of the same map $P^{r-2}|_V\to K|_V$ as for $Q$. These image identifications can be checked by the local-lifting criterion (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting]: a section is a boundary exactly when it locally lifts through that same incoming map. Hence the quotients, and the map induced by $i$, agree. In degree $r$, $H^r(Q)=0$ and $H^r(P|_V)=0$ because the restricted section $s|_V$ still splits $\delta|_V$. In degrees $j>r$ both complexes have zero terms. Thus $f$ induces isomorphisms in every degree and $Q^j=0$ for $j>r-1$. Only the two highest degrees were changed, so the argument applies for every integer $r$ without any lower bound.

Step 5: cohomology checked in each degree (r-2 kernel unchanged, r-1 cycles = K with the same boundaries, r split, above r zero). Edge cases: empty X, P^r = 0, P^{r-1} = 0, identity pair, rank 0, nonreduced X, unbounded below.
